3. The prosecution case briefly is that the Sub-Divisional Engineer (buildings). P.W.D. Natore used to purchase fuel for using in the motor vehicles of the Department on credit from M/s. Rohee Syndicate. Natore by issuing credit slips from his office. The credit/requisition slips contained three portions out of which one portion was kept in the office of the Sub-Divisional Engineer and the remaining two portions were sent to the Manager, M/s. Rohee Syndicate for supplying fuel etc. The requisition slips were used to be written by the appellant Kh. Md. Shamsul Islam and signed by the Sub-Divisional Engineer. Requisition slip No. 2370 was issued by P.W. 5 (SDE) for supply of three gallons of Diesel on credit but at the time of preparation of the bill the figure 1 (one) was inserted before the figure 3(three) in the portion which was submitted with the bill. Another requisition slip No. 878 dated 28.11.75 for 8 gallons of Diesel was similarly interpolated by inserting the figure 1(one) before the figure 8(eight). Requisition slip No. 2367 dated 15.11.75 was issued for 25 gallons of Diesel etc. but two gallons of mobil were inserted in the slip while the bill was submitted. The Sub-Divisional Engineer issued requisition slip No. 2371 dated 23.11.75 for supply of 8 gallons of Diesel on credit but it was not entered in the, log-book maintained by the driver of the Vehicle. He also is-sued requisition slip No. 28 2363 dated 4.11.75 for 40 gallons of Diesel and 2 gallons of Mobil but one gallon of gear oil was inserted in the requisition slip while the bill was submitted. Further case of the prosecution is that the appellant Mohammad Hossain sent a bill Ext. 6 for payment of the amount in respect of the price of Diesel. Mobil etc. which were supplied on the basis of the requisition slips referred to above. Upon scrutiny the aforesaid interpolations were detected in the requisition slips and the Superintending Engineer brought the matter to the notice of the District Anti-Corruption Officer. Rajshahi vide his Memo dated 5.1.76 and ultimately the appellants were put on trial in the aforesaid Special case. 

 8. At the hearing of the appeals. Mr. Md. Ozair Farooq, learned Advocate-on-Record of appellant Kh. Md. Shamsul Islam submitted that although the appellant was convicted for an offence of forgery made in the requisition slips for making unlawful gain, the total amount was a paltry one i.e. Tk. 561.40 paisa and that also could not be misappropriated because of detection of the foregery before the bills could be passed for payment. He also submitted that there was nothing on record to show that he had actually made any gain or indulged in such practices of interpolation in the requisition slips earlier. The appellant was then aged about 55 years and at present about 70 years and he also lost his job. Upon these facts, the Court may substantially reduce the sentence. Mr. Farooq submitted on compassionate ground.
